indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or reported, so the word for route is taken by its sound

parts.note: a course is a route taken

explanation.surface: A traveller warns that the road ahead is said to be bumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse and rough are synonyms, both describing a texture or manner lacking smoothness or refinement.

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of crowded is taken

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

explanation.surface: A sharp customer stands at first in a packed pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is a rigid rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and bright both describe someone intelligent and quick-witted.

clue.text: Take choir, for a change, for something to eat

indicators.note: for a change means altered, so the letters of take choir are rearranged

explanation.surface: A director chooses to lead the choir to vary their routine, rewarded with a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: The artichoke is an edible thistle-like vegetable, eaten for its leaves and heart.

clue.text: Sleeveless garment — team's leader is after one

indicators.note: is after means this letter comes after the word for one

parts.note: single means one, alone

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of team's

explanation.surface: The captain is after one vest, perhaps for the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest worn by athletes or as underwear.

clue.text: Fish bones across middle of jetty

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the surgeon's letters span the central letter of jetty

parts.note: Bones (from sawbones) is slang for a surgeon or doctor

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the five-letter word jetty

explanation.surface: An angler describes fish skeletons lying across the centre of a pier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' looks like part of the fish, but it is old slang for a surgeon (from sawbones). The T from the middle of JETTY goes inside SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish prized for its roe, caviar.

parts.note: services here are tennis serves, and the problem is an arm ailment, not a fault in public services

explanation.walkthrough: 'Services' suggests utilities or public provision; in tennis a serve is a service, and the strain injures a player's elbow.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a painful inflammation of the forearm tendons, commonly caused by repeated strokes in racket sports.

parts.note: a ref (referee) is an arbiter in sport
re means regarding, concerning
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: News about a referee concerning a hospital in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh a web page or display is to update it with the latest data.

parts.note: even can mean still, as in 'even better' or 'still better'

explanation.surface: There is still time to get the desired outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: An event can mean an outcome or result, as in 'in the event' meaning as it turned out.

clue.text: I trust an eccentric, one espousing nudity

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or unconventional, so the letters of I trust an are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for an oddball who believes in going unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist is a nudist, someone who advocates going without clothes.

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
to nurse is to tend a patient

explanation.surface: An instruction to stretch out a retired nurse, perhaps after a long shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend a limb is to straighten it out fully from a bent position.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an effect is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a well-liked result is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'in effect' means in reality or virtually, i.e. really, as a matter of practical fact.

clue.text: European university with typical wild trees

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of typical are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A continental campus has grounds full of the usual untamed trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Note the plural of eucalyptus is formed the Latin way, ending in -I.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalypti are Australian gum trees, the plural of eucalyptus.

clue.text: £25, say, for mail service long ago

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
to express something is to say it

explanation.surface: Paying twenty-five pounds, for example, for an old-fashioned postal delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is British money slang for £25; 'say' looks like an example marker but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pony Express was a relay of horse riders carrying mail across the American West in 1860-61.

clue.text: Register one with lease? Not initially

indicators.note: not initially means lose the first letter, so the opening letter of the tenant word is dropped

parts.note: a renter holds a property on a lease

explanation.surface: A form asks whether a leaseholder signed up, with an awkward afterthought.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a name or item is to record or register it, as in a list or ledger.

clue.text: Anxious, one outside shelter with husband beset by birds

indicators.note: outside means the word one goes around the shelter word

parts.note: taken as written
a tent is a simple shelter

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the birds enclose the husband letter

parts.note: rooks are birds of the crow family
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: A lone camper fears for her husband as birds gather round.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenterhook held cloth stretched taut on a drying frame, hence the sense of strained suspense.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on tenterhooks is an idiom for being in suspense, nervously waiting for news.

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A persistent mark on fabric that needs cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate and stubborn are synonyms for refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: Assistance provided by government — its data broadcast about energy

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the energy letter
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of its data are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A government shares its statistics on energy policy.
explanation.definitionFit: State aid is public financial support given by a government to firms or sectors.

parts.note: Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell were the pen names of the three Brontë sisters; the record is a well-known popular song

explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte, Emily and Anne Brontë first published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell, so they were three Bells; the answer is also the title of a hit song recorded by the Browns and by Edith Piaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a famous song recording, here jokily credited to the trio of pseudonymous literary sisters.

clue.text: Spooner's a lot more complex? Crazy

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: way means a lot, as in 'way more'
higher means more advanced or complex, as in higher maths

explanation.surface: A puzzle-solver complains a clue is far more complicated, and calls it mad.
explanation.walkthrough: WAY HIGHER spoken with initial sounds swapped becomes HAY WIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go haywire is an idiom for going out of control, behaving erratically or madly.

clue.text: Siren of traditional tales on the French island

parts.note: lore is the body of traditional stories
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A mermaid from old stories lives on an island owned by France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the Rhine siren of German legend who lured boatmen onto the rock.

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the skilful word surrounds the city letters

parts.note: deft means skilful, expert
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A skilled guide shows visitors round a city set in a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' reads as a sandy noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To defect is to abandon one's side or country, i.e. to desert it.

parts.note: okay means fine or all right

explanation.surface: A sommelier says the serving temperature is fine for a bottle from Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay (Tokaji) is a famous sweet dessert wine from the Tokaj region of Hungary.

indicators.note: some means part of, so the answer lies inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: A Baltic chess great is described as something of a gambler.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Keres really was an Estonian grandmaster, so 'Estonian' both hides the letters and fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Keres (1916-75) was a leading chess grandmaster, several times a world title candidate.

clue.text: New rope I ordered to hold large overhead cable, perhaps

indicators.note: to hold means the rearranged letters contain the large letter
ordered means arranged into a new sequence, so the letters of new rope I are rearranged

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A rigger orders a fresh rope to support a big cable strung overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like it describes the rope, but its letters belong in the anagram fodder with ROPE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A power line carrying electricity is typically an overhead cable slung between pylons; 'perhaps' admits buried ones exist.

clue.text: Loyalty programme? Form of realism I injected

indicators.note: injected means put inside, so the letter I goes into the reshaped letters of realism
form of means a reshaped version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic adds a personal touch to a type of realistic art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' rearranges REALISM into ARMILES, and 'injected' puts I inside it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Air Miles is a reward scheme in which customers earn points toward flights, a classic customer loyalty scheme.

parts.note: pleas are appeals or requests

indicators.note: close to means the last letter, so the end of umpire is taken

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: like the appeals that ring out near the umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' reads as 'similar to', but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to be to their liking, as in 'do as you please', i.e. as you like.

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors in the British police
per se is Latin for in itself, essentially

explanation.surface: A statement that police officers are fundamentally apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse is to scatter or break up, i.e. to separate, as a crowd does.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to absorb food or information
second meaning: a summary or compilation of material

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the noun are pronounced differently but spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as a verb for absorbing or assimilating and a noun for a condensed summary.
